Adversarial review of #204 (vendor claw governance, pin claw `cb83def3`). There were 18 findings, each checked by two independent verifiers. Fixes are on the PR branch unless marked otherwise.

**Fixed in #204**

- **The two validators disagreed on timestamps.** The schema's `range: datetime` makes the closed gate require an RFC 3339 date-time (jsonschema `format: date-time`). The Python validator checked only the `20YY-` prefix, and the docs said "ISO 8601". The Python validator now uses the same jsonschema `FormatChecker`, and the schema description and `CLAUDE.md` state the real contract. `rfc3339-validator` is now a declared dependency, since without it jsonschema silently skips the format check.
- **Tests passed for the wrong reason.** The `{"timestamp": "2026-09-28"}` list case and the `26-…` year case were rejected by the date-time format, not by the rule they named; both are replaced. New cases:
  - a year-guarded non-date-time;
  - a missing timestamp;
  - an explicit null history;
  - a bad second event.

  Mutation-checked:

  | Mutant | Tests that fail |
  |---|---|
  | missing timestamp accepted | 1 |
  | `get()` instead of `in` | 1 |
  | first event only | 1 |
  | Python date-time check dropped | 4 |
  | `range: datetime` → `string` | 4 |
- **Shared-shape wording.** "The fleet's shared CurationEvent shape" was not true: NaturalProductMech's differs. The text now says it matches TaxonMech's, and that what every Mech shares is the year guard.
- **Backlog hint.** The text moved into `prompts/backlog-loop-local.md` told the agent to pick a pathway and draft a record, which contradicts the canonical loop's "recommend, then pause" rule and its data-mutation rule. It is rewritten as PathwayMech's gates and data rules.
- **`CLAUDE.md` named only 5 of the 14 governed files.** It now lists all 14. It also says that `scripts/deep_research_contract.py` is claw's provider contract, not the local `pathwaymech-deep-research-contract` checker.
- **`vendored-sync` had no local entry point.** A new `just vendored-check` recipe fills that gap, and the README mentions it.

**Fixed in the PR description**

- `vendored-sync` runs on pushes to `main`, not on every push, and not every Mech has this workflow.
- `oaklib` is needed because the vendored tests import it. PathwayMech's id-label gate itself is still not configured, which is why claw declares `id_label_validation` disabled.

**Claw side, tracked in culturebotai-claw**

Merging #204 makes claw's recorded PathwayMech declarations false:
- The `id_label_validation` and `curation_history` reasons claim `scripts/validate_id_label_correspondence.py` and `src/pathwaymech/schema/history.yaml` are absent. claw's `test_manifest_reason_claims.py` then goes red against a fetched checkout.
- The `deep_research` prose and the `vendored_sync` comment are also stale.
- claw's merge-queue policy lists only `qc` for PathwayMech, so `vendored-sync` would never be required.

These need a claw PR after #204 merges.

**Not fixed**

- A timestamp with a trailing newline passes both validators. The year-guard pattern `^20[0-9]{2}-` is fixed byte-for-byte by the vendored `tests/test_curation_timestamp_schema.py`, and jsonschema's date-time check uses a `$`-anchored regex. Both validators agree on it, so nothing disagrees; tightening it is a claw canon change.
- The vendored id-label tests exercise only fakes. This is by design until the gate is configured for PathwayMech; claw records `id_label_validation` as disabled.
title: Review of #204: timestamp contract, test isolation, governed-file docs, and claw-side follow-ups

body:
- **Only renderer-owned files are checked.** A hand-made page, a stray `records/*.htm`, or a deleted `style.css` all pass, and the workflow publishes everything under `pages/`.
- **Colliding slugs pass.** Two record ids with one slug (`X/1`, `X_1`) produce one page, and the check reports the site current.
- **Case-only renames break on macOS.** On a case-insensitive filesystem, changing an id only in case makes a render delete the page it just wrote, or leave the old-case name that fails on Linux.
- **A `\r` fails the check straight after a render.** A carriage return in a label or description makes the check fail even though the page was just rendered: the file is read with newline translation.

body:
- **A skipped run is recorded as a deployment.** The current-main guard is a step inside the job that declares `environment: github-pages`. When it declines, the job still finishes green, and GitHub records a successful deployment at the run's commit (main's head, for `workflow_run`). claw's `fleet_pages_status.py` then reports the site as CURRENT while it still serves an older commit.
- **An older run can cancel the newest.** With `concurrency: pages`, a later-arriving run for an older commit X replaces the queued run for main's head Y, then skips itself because X is not main. Y is never published.
- **Dispatch skips CI.** `workflow_dispatch` publishes main without checking that "Build and test" passed, contrary to the workflow's own header comment.

body:
Adversarial review of PR #165 found that the generic WikiPathways importer drops central reactions and mechanistic edges that are represented through GPML anchors or grouped side participants.

## Problem

`gpml_to_pathway_record()` only walks direct `Interaction` endpoints whose `Point GraphRef` values are supported `DataNode`s. That misses three common WikiPathways shapes:

- side substrates, side products, and catalysts that connect to a central interaction through an `<Anchor>`;
- group graph nodes that point at child `DataNode`s through `GroupRef`;
- anchored conversions with one supported endpoint and one CAS-only or otherwise unsupported endpoint.

On `Sc_NAD_salvage_pathway_V_WP171_20260901.gpml`, the old importer emitted 3 reaction nodes and 6 direct ChEBI edges. It lost the two central nicotinamide conversions, every catalyst, and every anchored side substrate/product group even though the supported ChEBI and SGD identifiers are present in the GPML.

## Expected

- Expand supported members of GPML `<Group>` nodes in interaction endpoints.
- Map `<Anchor>` graph IDs back to the central interaction that owns them.
- Treat side arrows into a central anchor as consumed participants, side arrows out of a central anchor as produced participants, and `mim-catalysis` arrows into an anchor as `catalyzes` edges.
- Keep anchored central conversions if at least one direct endpoint is supported, while still skipping unrelated one-sided arrows to unsupported adjacent pathway callouts.

## Acceptance

- The WikiPathways fixture covers grouped ChEBI side substrates, grouped SGD catalysts, bare numeric ChEBI identifiers, and an anchored conversion with a CAS-only endpoint.
- `pathwaymech-import-wikipathways /private/tmp/wp-Saccharomyces_cerevisiae/Sc_NAD_salvage_pathway_V_WP171_20260901.gpml` emits 5 reaction nodes and 26 ChEBI/SGD mechanistic edges.
- `just test`, `just validate`, `just lint`, and `git diff --check` pass.
title: Import WikiPathways anchor and group-member GPML edges

body:
Adversarial review of PR #165 found that rootless WikiPathways GPML files can seed non-canonical PathwayMech IDs.

## Problem

`pathwaymech-import-wikipathways` currently falls back to `WikiPathways:{path.stem}` when a GPML has no top-level `<Xref Database="WikiPathways" ... />`.

Some current WikiPathways dumps, including `Sc_NAD_salvage_pathway_V_WP171_20260901.gpml`, carry the stable accession in `Version="WP171_r20260901073100"` and in the filename instead. Those sources import as pseudo IDs such as:

`WikiPathways:Sc_NAD_salvage_pathway_V_WP171_20260901`

## Expected

- Prefer an explicit root WikiPathways `<Xref>` when present.
- Otherwise extract `WP\d+` from the GPML `Version` attribute.
- As the final WikiPathways fallback, extract `WP\d+` from the input filename before using the whole stem.
- Keep the existing whole-stem fallback for fixtures or unusual local files with no accession token.

## Acceptance

- The `WPTEST` fixture covers a rootless GPML with a `Version` accession.
- A filename like `Sc_NAD_salvage_pathway_V_WP171_20260901.gpml` falls back to `WikiPathways:WP171`.
- `pathwaymech-import-wikipathways /private/tmp/wp-Saccharomyces_cerevisiae/Sc_NAD_salvage_pathway_V_WP171_20260901.gpml` emits `id: WikiPathways:WP171`.
title: Extract canonical WikiPathways accessions from rootless GPML

## Finding

PR #124 adds `data/pathways/dolichyl-glucosyl-phosphate-biosynthesis.yaml` with a description that says:

> PGM1, PGM2, or YHL012W phosphoglucomutase activity

That misassigns `YHL012W` to the phosphoglucomutase step.

## Evidence

- `SGD:S000001004` / `YHL012W Scer` enables `gomodel:YeastPathways_PWY3O-1565/6a4c244800003258` in `edge-022`.
- `gomodel:YeastPathways_PWY3O-1565/6a4c244800003258` is labeled `UTP:glucose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase activity`.
- The normalized SGD GO-CAM projection has the same activity as `GO:0003983` with `CHEBI:46398`, `CHEBI:58601`, and `CHEBI:15378` inputs.

The graph edges are source-faithful; only the summary sentence needs to move `YHL012W` from the phosphoglucomutase clause to the UTP-coupling clause.

## Fix

- Update `data/pathways/dolichyl-glucosyl-phosphate-biosynthesis.yaml` so the description keeps `PGM1` / `PGM2` on the `D-glucopyranose 6-phosphate -> alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate` step and puts `YHL012W` with `UGP1` on the UTP-coupling step.
- Rerun `just render-pages`.
- Rerun `just validate`, `just test`, `just lint`, and `git diff --check`.
title: Fix YHL012W step in dolichyl glucosyl phosphate description

body:
Adversarial review of PR #77 found that the first version of `data/pathways/spermidine-biosynthesis-i.yaml` cited broad current GO-CAM API fragments such as `"has_input":[` plus a standalone ChEBI term.

Those snippets do not bind each ChEBI participant to a specific `has_input` or `has_output` assertion, and repeated terms such as `CHEBI:57443` and `CHEBI:15378` make the evidence ambiguous.

Replace the generic API-list evidence with exact fact-level GO-CAM quotes for each molecular association so every collapsed PathwayMech edge is tied to:

- the GO-CAM activity node,
- the exact RO predicate,
- the local GO-CAM molecule/controller individual, and
- that individual's ChEBI or SGD type.
title: Quote edge-specific GO-CAM facts for spermidine

The EcoCyc MG1655 strain is only one `<species>` entry; the same source frame also lists *Klebsiella aerogenes* / NCBI 548. Update the curated record to use `NCBITaxon:2` / Bacteria for the pathway-level microbial scope, then rerender and revalidate PR #63.

body: PR #57 adversarial review found that data/pathways/d-arabinose-degradation-i.yaml scopes MetaCyc:DARABCAT-PWY to generic NCBITaxon:562 even though the exact two-step DARABISOM-RXN // D-RIBULOKIN-RXN route is evidenced for Escherichia coli B. The K-12 pathway is the separate four-step MetaCyc:DARABCATK12-PWY route, so the DARABCAT record should use NCBITaxon:37762 / Escherichia coli B or another directly evidenced taxon.
title: Scope DARABCAT-PWY to Escherichia coli B

body: PR #57 adversarial review found that the DARABCAT D-ribulokinase step uses RHEA:17604, Rhea's bidirectional child, while the graph asserts catabolic D-ribulose + ATP consumption and D-ribulose 5-phosphate + ADP + H(+) production. RHEA:17602 is the left-to-right child of RHEA:17601 and should replace RHEA:17604 in the local reaction, edge endpoints, evidence reference, and generated page.
title: Use the left-to-right Rhea D-ribulokinase child in DARABCAT

> The Escherichia coli pabA and pabB genes have been overexpressed separately and in tandem.

That quote only establishes overexpression. It does not establish that the PabA/PabB enzyme complex catalyzes aminodeoxychorismate synthesis or the RHEA:11673 conversion of chorismate + L-glutamine to 4-amino-4-deoxychorismate + L-glutamate.

Replace it with a primary-paper snippet that directly supports the specific catalysis edge, or drop the weak primary evidence and leave the Rhea EC assertion alone.

## Problem

PR #12 adds `data/pathways/l-cysteine-biosynthesis-i.yaml` with participant `CHEBI:29919` labeled as `hydrogen sulfide`.

`CHEBI:29919` is the hydrosulfide anion, while neutral hydrogen sulfide is `CHEBI:16136`. The pathway should keep the Rhea-backed `CHEBI:29919` participant for `RHEA:14830`, but the local participant label should match the ChEBI entity that downstream joins will resolve.

## Fix

- Relabel `CHEBI:29919` to `hydrosulfide` in `data/pathways/l-cysteine-biosynthesis-i.yaml`.
- Regenerate `pages/` with `just render-pages`.
- Rerun `just validate`, `just test`, `just lint`, and `git diff --check`.
title: Correct cysteine hydrosulfide label

Found during adversarial review of PR #4.

The data/pathways/l-arginine-degradation-iv.yaml record currently represents MetaCyc:ARGDEG-III-PWY with the Enterococcus faecalis putrescine-carbamoyltransferase/carbamate-kinase arm:

- NCBITaxon:1351
- EC:2.1.3.6
- EC:2.7.2.2
- RHEA:21938
- RHEA:10154
- PMID:17028272

That is the lactic-bacterial agmatine-to-ATP route, not the MetaCyc L-arginine degradation IV amidase route. The ARGDEG-III-PWY record should instead keep arginine decarboxylase and agmatine deiminase, then terminate with N-carbamoylputrescine amidase.

Acceptance:

- use Pseudomonas aeruginosa as the organism scope for this record
- replace the PTC / CK tail with EC:3.5.1.53 and direction-specific RHEA:22285
- add putrescine, ammonium, and CO2 products directly from RHEA:22285
- cite Pseudomonas amidase evidence with PMID:12634339
- regenerate pages and rerun validation
title: Correct ARGDEG-III-PWY to the amidase branch

body:
## Problem
The KGML importer passes a missing substrate/product name into the KEGG CURIE formatter. That formatter indexes the last whitespace-delimited token, so a partial or malformed KGML reaction participant raises IndexError before the importer can validate the resulting draft.

## Impact
One incomplete substrate or product can crash the whole KEGG import without an actionable PathwayMech validation message.

## Fix
Treat missing KGML names as unmappable participants, skip them, and cover this path with a regression test.
title: Skip unnamed KGML reaction participants

body:
## Problem
BioPAX physical entities and WikiPathways GPML data nodes can contain repeated graph or physical nodes that resolve to the same stable ChEBI, UniProtKB, EC, or GO CURIE. The new importers currently preserve one participant object per BioPAX physical-entity ref or GPML GraphId while edges already point at the stable CURIE.

## Impact
A real upstream pathway with the same compound rendered in two places can emit duplicate participant IDs and then fail PathwayMech YAML validation even though the edge endpoints themselves are valid.

## Fix
Emit unique participant records keyed by their stable CURIE while retaining all graph/physical-node-to-CURIE lookups for edge construction. Add regression tests for duplicated GPML DataNodes and BioPAX physical entities.
title: Deduplicate participant IDs in BioPAX and GPML imports
